**J**
Jacob and Israel is rightly called the Christian people, Ps. 52:8. Why a door is called *janua*, from Janus, Ps. 73:7. Fasting is so called as though from *inedia* (“starvation”), Ps. 34:16. Jonadab the priest commanded his sons to serve God soberly, Ps. 70, title. What “jubilation” or “jubilation-song” means, Ps. 32:3 and Ps. 46:1. Also Ps. 65:1. Also Ps. 88:15. The Jew is called an enemy and avenger, Ps. 8:3. The Jews are corrupt in understanding, Ps. 13:2. The Jews are called sons of strangers, Ps. 17:49. The Jews limp in faith, ibid. The Jews are called unicorns, Ps. 28:6. The Jews dwell in the circuit, that is, in the shell of the letter, Ps. 30:16. The Jews are outside the number, namely, of the righteous, Ps. 39:8. The iniquity of the Jews is upon the walls of Jerusalem, Ps. 54:10. The Jews profane God’s Testament, ibid. 23. The Jews falsely speak of the righteousness of the Law, Ps. 57:1. The Jews are obstinate like an asp, ibid., 4. The Jews are workers of iniquity, Ps. 58:2. The Jews will be converted to Christ at the end of the world, ibid. 7. The Jews were delivered into the hands of the sword, Ps. 62:9. The machinations of the Jews against Christ, Ps. 63:8. The Jews lied to God, Ps. 65:2. The Jews added iniquity upon iniquity, Ps. 68:32. The Jews are said to act against the Law, whereas the pagans are wicked, Ps. 70:5. The Jews and Israel now exist only in name, Ps. 75:1. The Jews are a crooked and provoking generation, Ps. 77:10. The Jews did not truly fear God, Ps. 84:10. The seat of the Jews is shattered, Ps. 88:43. The instability and begging of the Jews, Ps. 108:9. The Jews, like bees, made honey not for themselves but for others, Ps. 117:12. Judas the betrayer is called a son of iniquity, Ps. 88:22. Judas had a wife and children, Ps. 108:8. The saints are judged in equity, sinners in justice, Ps. 9:8 and Ps. 97:10. How the Christian asks to be judged by God, Ps. 42:1. Judgment was given to Christ according to his human nature, Ps. 71:1. The final judgment is compared to a storm, Ps. 82:14. What it means to swear deceitfully, Ps. 23:4. Swearing is fitting for God but forbidden to a human being, Ps. 88:4. “To swear” is understood in two ways, Ps. 108:106. What it means to reject God’s justice from oneself, Ps. 17 [Col. 1449]:25. What are called upright forms of justice, Ps. 18:9. God’s justice is to spare the penitent, Ps. 70:1. The righteous person is like a palm tree and like a cedar, Ps. 91:12. The young women with tambourines are sacred virgins, Ps. 67:27. Youth is called the newness of life, Ps. 42:4. Youth is the period when one fights against vices, Ps. 67:27.

## L

The lips of Christ are the two Testaments, Ps. 15:4. The lips of Christ are holy preachers, Ps. 39:12. The labor of the lips is falsehood, Ps. 139:10. What the pit means, Ps. 7:16. The pit signifies either this age or hell, Ps. 27:1. What the pit of misery and the mire of filth mean, Ps. 39:2. “Pit” is understood in various ways, Ps. 87:6. To rejoice in the Lord, not in oneself, Ps. 31:14. True joy is to believe rightly, Ps. 4:7. Laments are made at a funeral, Ps. 77:69. The snare of death is the guilt of original sin, Ps. 17:6. The snare is beside the way, not in the way, Ps. 118:110. God’s broad commandment is charity, Ps. 118:96. How the praise of God is always in our mouth, Ps. 33:1 and Ps. 34:32. The praise of God exists only among the saints, Ps. 47:9. To wash one’s hands in the blood of a sinner, Ps. 57:10. The bed is so called from chosen and soft grasses, Ps. 6:6. The Lawgiver is called the Antichrist, but falsely, Ps. 9:21. Both Christ and the devil are compared to a lion, Ps. 7:2. The immaculate Law of the Lord is Christ, Ps. 18:8. The mysteries of the Law are like melting wax, Ps. 21:15. The Law of your mouth is worth more than thousands of gold and silver, Ps. 118:71. The Law is not a stumbling-block to the good, ibid., 165. To be delivered from bloodguilt is to be absolved from sins, Ps. 50:15. The feet are delivered from falling not here, but in the age to come, Ps. 55:13. The earth enriched through Christ, Ps. 64:9. What the place of pasture means, Ps. 22:1. To speak with the mouth and not with the heart, Ps. 21:7. What it means to speak iniquity against God, Ps. 74:5. The light of God’s countenance is the sign of the cross and God’s grace, Ps. 4:7. Holy Scripture is a lamp for our paths, Ps. 118:105.

## M

What it means to magnify the Lord, Ps. 69:5. What kind of evil the Lord guards against, Ps. 120:7. What it means to command salvation for Jacob, Ps. 43:6. To establish the Testament forever, Ps. 110:8. To understand God’s commandments is to act according to them, Ps. 118:95. To pray in the morning is to live in a life illuminated by good conduct, Ps. 5:3. Morning signifies joy, evening sadness, Ps. 64:8. Morning is the time of pardon, Ps. 142:9. Who are the meek and gentle, Ps. 24:10 and Ps. 36:11. The sea signifies the nations, Ps. 88:25 and Ps. 94:5. How the martyrs were heard, Ps. 33:17. It is not punishment but the cause that makes martyrs, Ps. 34:26. The martyrs were like sheep for slaughter, Ps. 43:13 and 24. The martyrs were joyful in their passion, Ps. 118:159. The morning reception is the time of resurrection, Ps. 21, title. One must rise at midnight to praise God, Ps. 118:62. To meditate on God’s Law all day, ibid., 97. Meditation on the Law consists more in practice than in reading, Ps. 118:77. To remember God upon one’s bed in prosperity, Ps. 62:7. Who remembers God’s commandments, Ps. 102:18. One who remembers God’s judgments does not sin, Ps. 118:52. The sons of men are liars on the scales, Ps. 61:9. The table signifies sacred Scripture, Ps. 22:6. The table made for the Jews became a snare, Ps. 68:27. [Col. 1450] *Metabole* is a certain figure of speech, Ps. 5:1. The wonders of the Law are spiritual mysteries, Ps. 118:18 and 129. Mercy of the heart is compassion expressed in action, Ps. 24:6. To ask mercy from God is the best defense of the guilty, Ps. 50:1. God’s mercy is better than lives, Ps. 62:4. Mercy and judgment, or truth, are present in all God’s works, Ps. 110:1. God’s mercy is great above the heavens, Ps. 107:4. A monk—that is, a solitary person—separated from every sin, Ps. 67:6. The eternal mountains are called prophets and apostles, Ps. 75:4. The holy mountains likewise are called prophets and apostles, Ps. 86:1. Smoking mountains, Ps. 143:6. The death of sinners is most evil, Ps. 33:21. The death of martyrs is not death but the shadow of death, Ps. 43:21. The death of martyrs is precious and life-giving, Ps. 115:5. Christ’s death is called a sitting, Ps. 138:1. One who does not keep God’s commandments is called dead, Ps. 118:17. Who is called dead to the world, Ps. 142:4. How Moses and Aaron are interpreted, Ps. 76:20. Why this world is called the sea, Ps. 64:6. This world is a place of pilgrimage, Ps. 118:54. This world is called night, Ps. 19:55. This world is called a desert, Ps. 135:16. This world is called a cave, Ps. 141, title.

## N

Necessities are called adversities or venial sins, Ps. 24:18. Necessity, placed in *nece* (“death”), that is, in sin, Ps. 39:9. No one can endure God’s judgment without mercy, Ps. 142:2. Wickedness is voluntary malice, Ps. 36:8. God does not know what perishes; he knows what remains, Ps. 1:7. *Nimis* (“exceedingly”) is explained in two ways, Ps. 108:29. Excessiveness in the divine warfare is a virtue, Ps. 118:4. The name of God is “Lord,” or “He Is,” Ps. 9:10. Christ’s name remains before the sun, Ps. 71:17. The new degree is the mystery of the Trinity, Ps. 127, title. The exceedingly bright clouds are the divine utterances or the apostles, Ps. 17:14. Clouds are understood as prophets, Ps. 56:13. Clouds are called preachers, Ps. 76:16 and Ps. 88:7.

## O

What it means to sleep in death, Ps. 11:4. What it means to forget God, Ps. 9:18 and Ps. 49:23. The sinner craftily watches the righteous person, Ps. 36:12. To kill sinners, Ps. 138:18. What it means to lower one’s eyes toward the earth, Ps. 16:12. The eye is so called as though it were “swifter than light,” Ps. 6:7. To hate discipline, Ps. 49:18. To hate God’s enemies, Ps. 138:20–21. To offer gifts around, Ps. 75:11. Og—that is, “conclusion”—is the devil, Ps. 134:11 and Ps. 135:20. The sinner’s oil is flattery, Ps. 140:6. The cauldron of our hope is the tribulation of the saints, Ps. 59:8. The Jews are called wild asses, Ps. 103:12. Holy works exist only in the Church, Ps. 133:3. God crowns his works in us, Ps. 144:9. The good are a reproach to the wicked, Ps. 68:13. One must pray for enemies, Ps. 6:10. To pray with outstretched hands, Ps. 142:6. Prayer and supplication differ, Ps. 38:16. To establish Christ’s Testament over sacrifices, Ps. 49:6. What it means for the mouth to abound in wickedness, Ps. 69:20. The bones signify strength of mind, Ps. 6:2 and Ps. 34:11. Also Ps. 50:9.

## P

The soul’s bread is tears, Ps. 41:3. The bread of sorrow likewise means tears, Ps. 126:3. Parable and propositions differ, Ps. 77:2. What a parable means, Ps. 68:14. Paradise is the land of the living, Ps. 14:7. Who is ready for God’s commandments, Ps. 118:60. Monks are compared to sparrows, Ps. 103:18. Our fathers are the prophets and apostles, Ps. 43:1. [Col. 1451] The patriarchs are called Christ’s, Ps. 104:15. The apostle Paul is called Benjamin the youth, Ps. 67:29. The poor and the needy differ, Ps. 36:15. The poor are Christians who despise the riches of the world, Ps. 68:38. Who are God’s poor, Ps. 71:2. Heavenly peace “in unity,” that is, unchanging, Ps. 4:9. What it means to have peace with the Lord, Ps. 65:2. Those who do not obey priests sin, Ps. 77:36. Sin is committed in three ways: in thought, word, and deed, Ps. 1:1. Sinners differ from the righteous and from the impious, Ps. 1:6. Sinners are called cattle, Ps. 8:9. Sinners are erased like mud, Ps. 17:46. Sinners are thrown away like dust, Ps. 34:6. Sinners fail like smoke, Ps. 67:2. Sinners do not have peace in their conscience, Ps. 72:3. What it means for sinners to exalt their horn, Ps. 74:4. Hidden and alien sin differ, Ps. 18:13. Our sins are many, Ps. 24:12. What it means for sin not to be imputed, Ps. 31:2. Original sin is drawn from Adam, Ps. 50:6. Abraham’s pilgrimages, Ps. 104:13. We are all pilgrims here, Ps. 38:17. The foot of the soul is love, Ps. 9:16. The foot is called the mind’s affection, Ps. 35:12. One must ask God constantly, Ps. 118:124. What the petition of the heart means, Ps. 36:4. Pharaoh signifies the devil, Ps. 134:9. Why philosophers are called the fish of the sea, Ps. 8:8. The writings of philosophers are nothing compared with sacred Scripture, Ps. 140:7. What the fatness of the soul means, Ps. 62:6. Who are the fat ones of the earth, Ps. 21:32. To clap the hands allegorically means to perform good works, Ps. 46:1. Why the penitent is compared to a pelican, Ps. 101:7. To place a stumbling-block before a brother, Ps. 49:21. To set one’s mouth in heaven, Ps. 72:9. The gates of death are the devil and the heretic, Ps. 9:14. The eternal gates are faith and charity, Ps. 23:7. The gate is Christ. The gates are the apostles and prophets, Ps. 117:19. Preachers in the Church are like towers, Ps. 47:11. Who are transgressors, Ps. 118:158. Evil princes are persecutors and devils, ibid., 161. In this world the faithful are a portent to sinners, Ps. 70:8. Portents are so called as though they were “speaking further,” Ps. 77:48 and Ps. 104:26. The prophets often use the past for the future, Ps. 43:9. Why the prophets are called seers, Ps. 88:19. All human beings are our neighbors, Ps. 14:4. To play the psaltery and to sing differ, Ps. 20:13 and Ps. 26:11. What it means to play the psaltery wisely, Ps. 46:7. What it means to play to the Lord on the cithara, Ps. 97:7. What psalmody means, Ps. 136:7. What a psalm of a song means, Ps. 74, around the title. A psalm differs from a song, Ps. 4, around the title. God is praised in a psalm more by deeds than by words, Ps. 17:53. How the psaltery and cithara differ, Ps. 32:2 and Ps. 17:24. The psaltery is an image of the Lord’s body, Ps. 48:4. Our deeds are compared to the psaltery, Ps. 107:1. Christians are called children because of simplicity and purity of mind, Ps. 112:1. Christ is called a child because of the purity of innocence, Ps. 68:21. A human being who is earthly and impious is called dust, Ps. 1:5. The pupil of the eye is so called as though it were “little” (*pusilla*), Ps. 16:9. The short time is what remains until the day of judgment, Ps. 36:10. The pit of destruction is the depth of Gehenna, Ps. 54:26. “Pit” is understood in both a good and a bad sense, Ps. 68:9.

## Q

To seek falsehood, Ps. 4:3. To seek God’s face, Ps. 23:6. To seek evils, Ps. 70:14. To seek food for oneself from God, Ps. 103:22. *Quis* (“who”) is often used to indicate rarity, Ps. 23:3.

[Col. 1452]

## R

The frog signifies the loquacity of heretics, Ps. 77:50. Who are upright of heart, Ps. 63:11 and Ps. 124:4. Any good Christians are called kings, Ps. 101:16. The kingdom of all ages, Ps. 144:13. The remnant of the Jews is to be converted to Christ, Ps. 20:12. The remnants of the righteous remain; those of the impious perish, Ps. 36:39–40. To remember is to return to the Lord through repentance, Ps. 21:29. The rebuke of the kidneys, Ps. 15:7. The creeping things of the sea, that is, of this world, are demons, Ps. 103:26. The soul’s rest is a good conscience, Ps. 114:7. God regards sins in one way and the human being in another, Ps. 32:13. There are two resurrections: one from vices, the other into eternal life, Ps. 19:9. There are four kinds of recompense, Ps. 27:6. Who is called king and giant by comparison, Ps. 32:16. A king sins against God alone, but a commoner against God and the king, Ps. 50:5. The buckthorn is a kind of thorn, rough with prickles but pleasing in flower, Ps. 57:9. The righteous will laugh at sinners, Ps. 51:6. The streams are called apostles, Ps. 64:11. *Rogare* (“to ask”) is used for “to inquire,” Ps. 121:6. The dew of Hermon is called divine Scripture, Ps. 132:3. Ruin comes from the disputation of heretics, Ps. 143:17.

## S

What it means to sacrifice voluntarily, Ps. 53:6. The sacrifice of the Church is the offering of Christ’s body and blood, Ps. 19:3. The sacrifices of bulls are useful if they are distributed to the poor, Ps. 49:14. The sacrifice of praise is to die to the world and be offered to Christ, ibid., 15. Our sacrifice ought to be drenched not with blood but with tears, Ps. 50:18. The sacrifice of righteousness is Christ’s passion, Ps. 50:18. The evening sacrifice, Ps. 140:2. Christ’s arrows are sharp because they pierce hearts in order to heal them, Ps. 44:7. The willow is an unfruitful tree, Ps. 136:2. Solomon is a type of Christ, Ps. 71, title. The Lord saves human beings and animals, Ps. 35:7. What it means to be saved for nothing, Ps. 55:7. The saints are called heavens, in which God dwells, Ps. 2:4. The saints distinguish vows, Ps. 75:12. The saints are like deer, Ps. 140:10. Christ’s blood purifies; it does not make bloody, Ps. 129:7. What it means to ask wisely, Ps. 21:2. Wisdom concerns divine mysteries; prudence concerns conduct, Ps. 48:3. In Greek, “stumbling-block” (*scandalum*) signifies “left,” Ps. 105:34. It is not permissible to scrutinize God’s Law among the wicked, Ps. 118:115. The shield is so called as though it were “sculpted” (*sculptum*), Ps. 34:2. God crowns with a shield, Ps. 102:4. The second day of the week is the Catholic Church, Ps. 47, title. The saints are called God’s seats, Ps. 121:5. The seed of Jacob and the seed of Israel, Ps. 21:24–25. Human deeds are called seed, Ps. 36:26 and Ps. 111:1. The paths of righteousness are love of God and neighbor, Ps. 22:3. A path (*semita*) is so called as though it were a “half-way” (*semivia*), Ps. 24:4 and Ps. 118:35. Old age and advanced age differ, Ps. 70:19. The seven penitential psalms and the seven ways of remitting sins, Ps. 6:1. The seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, Ps. 11:7. To speak praise seven times a day, Ps. 118:164. “Sevenfold” signifies perfection, Ps. 78:13. The minds of unbelievers are called tombs, Ps. 97:12. A servant is so called from *servando* (“preserving”), Ps. 118:122. Who are the servants of the Lord, Ps. 113:1. Shiloh signifies the priesthood of Aaron rejected by God, Ps. 77:66. Who is called singular, Ps. 140:11. [Col. 1453] Zion designates the Church, Ps. 2:6 and Ps. 9:11. Zion means “contemplation of divinity,” Ps. 19:2. Zion is a small hill near the temple of Jerusalem, Ps. 68:40. What the soul that thirsts for God does, Ps. 62:2. Our lots are in God’s hand, Ps. 30:18. What the beloved appearance of Jacob means, Ps. 46:4. Hope is called singular in the Church, Ps. 4:10. God is the hope of all the ends of the earth, Ps. 64:6. What it means to drive in a thorn, Ps. 31:4. The right spirit is renewed in us through Christ, Ps. 50:11. What the princely spirit is in us, ibid., 13. Who is subject to God, Ps. 61:1. In Christ, substance is possession of a good conscience, Ps. 38:11. *Sum* (“I am”) is the proper word of God, indicating the Trinity, Ps. 42:8. The proud are compared to cedars, Ps. 28:5. The proud are those who sin and refuse to make satisfaction, Ps. 118:118. Pride is the greatest offense, Ps. 18:14. What it means to supplant, Ps. 36:33. To rise before daylight, Ps. 126:3. To wait for the Lord all day, Ps. 24:5. The synagogue is the assembly of the rejected, Ps. 7:7.

## T

The tabernacle is so called from *taberna* and *coenaculum*, Ps. 14:1. God’s tabernacle is the Church or the heavenly dwelling, Ps. 42:3. The tents of sinners are the present life, Ps. 83:11. To keep silent about sins is evil, Ps. 31:3. Fat bulls are the fierce rulers of the Jews, Ps. 21:12. The day of judgment will be a violent storm, Ps. 49:4. The wondrous temple in righteousness is Christ or the Church, Ps. 64:5. The time of favor is the time of Christ’s incarnation or passion, Ps. 68:16. The evil time is the day of judgment, Ps. 36:20. What it means to tempt, Ps. 76:21. There are two kinds of temptation: one from God, the other from the devil, Ps. 25:2. “Slain earth” is spoken tropologically, Ps. 105:37. This world is a deserted, trackless, waterless land, Ps. 62:3. God is terrible to the kings of the earth, Ps. 75:12. Those who pursue earthly things are called earthborn, Ps. 48:2. In Scripture, “testament” is used for every covenant, Ps. 82:5. The two Testaments are joined through Christ, Ps. 84:11. The eternal Testament properly means the New Law, Ps. 104:10. How we ought to store up treasure, Ps. 38:19. Fear of the Lord is charity, or reverence mingled with dread, Ps. 18:10. The fear of God is useful and effective, Ps. 21:24. The fear of God has sweetness; human fear has bitterness, Ps. 33:11. The fear of God is twofold: servile and chaste, Ps. 118:63. The usefulness of titles in the psalms, Ps. 2, around the title. The torrent signifies Christ’s wisdom, Ps. 35:9. The torrents of iniquity are the crowd of wicked people disturbing the Church, Ps. 17:5. To be afflicted from the heart is to mourn one’s sins, Ps. 33:18. The tribes of the Lord are the testimony of Israel, Ps. 121:4. The Trinity of persons is indicated, Ps. 5:2. Sadness is twofold: evil sadness over the adversities of this world, and good sadness over sins, Ps. 42:5. Trope and tropology in Scripture, Ps. 3:6. [Col. 1454] When the Jews used to blow the trumpet, Ps. 80:3. What drawn-metal trumpets and horn trumpets signify, Ps. 97:7. Christ’s undivided tunic designates the unity of the Church, Ps. 21:19.

## U

What the shadow of death means, Ps. 106:14. The unicorn signifies the one Church of Christ, Ps. 77:75. The proud are called unicorns, Ps. 21:22. The Christian people are called one and poor, Ps. 24:17. The soul of Christ or the Church is called one, Ps. 34:20. “As far as the horn of the altar,” that is, as far as communion, Ps. 117:26. Usury is forbidden, Ps. 14:6 and Ps. 54:11. Spiritual usury exists in sinners, Ps. 71:14.

## V

Who are the vain, Ps. 25:4 and Ps. 51:7. Vanity is what is empty and superfluous, Ps. 30:7. Vanity is changeability of mind, Ps. 38:8. The works of worldly vanity are like spiders’ webs, ibid., 15. What the false vanities and insanities are, Ps. 39:6. The Law of Moses was veiled for the Jews, Ps. 118:135. What an harsh word means, Ps. 90:3. God’s word remains in heaven, that is, among the saints and angels, Ps. 118:89. The verse to be said at the end of life, Ps. 115:7. What the crown of the head means, Ps. 7:17. Evening signifies the present life, Ps. 29:6. Christ’s footprints are his apostles, Ps. 16:6. The ways of virtue are hard; the path of vices is easy, Ps. 16:5. The ways of the Lord are love of God and neighbor, Ps. 17:24. The way of God is hard but safe; the way of the earth is soft but full of robbers, Ps. 36:24. The ways of the Lord are the apostles and prophets, Ps. 127:1. What it means to brandish, Ps. 7:13. What it means to see the Lord’s will, Ps. 26:8. To keep watch for God at dawn, Ps. 62:1. The order and course of divine vengeance, Ps. 77:54. The vengeance that the Christian asks for is good, Ps. 78:11. The vineyard prefigures the Church, which grows through persecutions alone, Ps. 79:9. The Jewish vineyard was changed into a Christian one, ibid., 10. The wine of compunction is the virtue of repentance, Ps. 59:3. The rod of direction is the rule of equity in Christ’s judgment, Ps. 44:8. The rod of sinners is called the power of tyrants, Ps. 124:3. The virgin bears fruit a hundredfold, the widow sixtyfold, ibid., 16. Who are men of blood, Ps. 5:7 and Ps. 25:9. Also Ps. 54:27. What it means to act manfully, Ps. 30:31. What it means to visit with a rod, Ps. 88:32. What true life is, Ps. 118:77. Proud people are called the birds of heaven, Ps. 8:8. What voluntary sacrifices are, Ps. 118:108. God’s will is like a shield to us, Ps. 5:15. The desire of Christ’s lips was not defrauded, Ps. 20:2. The Lord’s face is against the wicked, Ps. 33:16.

## Z

Zeal is twofold, good and bad, Ps. 118:139. The Ziphites designate sinners flourishing in this world, Ps. 53, title.
